stem: What does a computer fundamentally do?

options.text: It creates electricity from nothing
It takes instructions, processes information, and produces results
It can think and feel like a human
It only stores files and photos

explanation_after: A computer is an instruction-following machine. It processes inputs into outputs — nothing more, nothing less. It does not think or feel.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a component of a computer?

options.text: CPU (processor)
Memory (RAM)
Imagination
Storage

explanation_after: Computers have CPU, RAM, and storage — all physical hardware. Imagination is a human quality. Computers only do what they are explicitly instructed to do.

stem: Why is the phrase 'computers are intelligent' misleading?

options.text: Because they are too slow
Because computers only follow exact instructions — they don't understand or reason
Because only robots can be intelligent
Because computers cannot do math

explanation_after: Computers execute instructions with no understanding. Even AI systems are sophisticated instruction-following — they don't 'understand' the way humans do. This distinction matters deeply when building AI systems.

stem: A friend says, "My computer decided to open a browser window by itself this morning." What actually happened?

options.text: The computer used free will to decide on its own
Some program — like a scheduled task or startup script — instructed it to open the browser; computers never act without instructions
The browser opened itself using intuition
It's impossible for a program to open another program automatically

explanation_after: Computers never 'decide' anything in the human sense. Every action — even one that looks spontaneous — traces back to some instruction: a scheduled task, a startup item, a background service. If it happened, code told it to happen.

stem: What is the key difference between a computer's hardware and its software?

options.text: Hardware is the physical machine; software is the instructions that tell the hardware what to do
They are two names for the same thing
Software is physical; hardware is a set of instructions
Hardware only matters for gaming computers, not laptops

explanation_after: Hardware (CPU, RAM, storage) is the physical machine that can only follow instructions — it does nothing on its own. Software is the set of instructions that gives hardware a purpose. The same hardware can run a word processor, a game, or a training script for a neural network, depending only on which software is loaded.

stem: Why can the exact same laptop run a word processor, a video game, and code that trains a neural network?

options.text: It has separate hidden chips built in for each possible use
Hardware just follows whatever instructions are loaded into it — the same general-purpose hardware executes completely different software, including ML training code, without needing to change
It can't — each of those requires different physical hardware
AI training requires special non-electronic hardware

explanation_after: This is the general-purpose nature of computers: the hardware doesn't know or care what the instructions are for. The same CPU that renders a game frame can execute a PyTorch training loop, because both are just sequences of instructions. This is exactly why software written once (like an ML framework) can run on ordinary consumer hardware.
